headline: Low interaction risk: no shared I/O or network paths are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no documented I/O surfaces and agent B has clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, and screen_capture all false, so there is no plausible default channel for A’s outputs to reach B as instructions. The pairwise pathway is therefore blocked by the profiles, not merely unobserved.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, file bridge, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF agent A is connected to an MCP or filesystem channel not shown in the profile, the verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not add a shared workspace or message bus without provenance checks.
Review any future connector for instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A reports network_egress:none and no data classes touched; agent B has no filesystem read/write, no browser, no subprocesses, and no network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound path, there is no documented route for sensitive data to leak between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access or outbound network access, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, the current no-leak conclusion no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline from external APIs.
Avoid mounting a shared directory between them.
Confirm no secrets are passed through manual copy/paste.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or network surface in the profile, while agent B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because neither agent can mutate the same shared resource, there is no documented capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF agent A gains filesystem or git write access, overlapping-write conflict must be reconsidered.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free coordination, the current assessment may change.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for both agents.
Do not place them on the same mutable repository.
Recheck permissions before any deployment change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B has no documented input channels that would let it consume A’s outputs automatically, and A has no documented output channel beyond its repo/docs presence. Without an ingestion path, B cannot treat A’s output as authoritative in the default configuration.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are wired into B’s prompt or task queue, cascading-error risk becomes relevant.
IF B is configured to act on external text without verification, reassess this finding.
mitigations: Require explicit human review before passing outputs between agents.
Do not auto-feed one agent’s text into the other.
Add a verification step if any future pipeline connects them.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress plus no filesystem access on B. With no identified regulated data flow, there is no documented residency, retention, or subject-rights mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdictional or retention policy not shown here, this conclusion may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document any future retention or residency requirements.
Review compliance before enabling new data flows.
